results.title: Head of Growth & Operations
results.description:
Headquarters: US

URL: https://openbase.ai/

Head of Growth & Operations — Openbase.ai

Full-time | Remote | Reports directly to the Founder

About Openbase

Openbase.ai is an AI gateway that helps developers and businesses access multiple AI models through one API. We simplify model access, routing, and usage management so teams can focus on building AI products.

Our MVP is ready. We are hiring a hands-on leader to own our go-to-market strategy, day-to-day business execution, and journey from launch to our first 10,000 users.

The opportunity

You will work directly with the founder to turn Openbase into a growing business with repeatable customer acquisition, strong retention, and disciplined operations.

You will own the commercial execution: finding our first customers, testing acquisition channels, improving onboarding, building partnerships, and organizing the people and systems needed to grow.

Our ambition is 10,000 users. Your responsibility is to build a credible, measurable path toward that goal, with clear milestones for activated developers, retained customers, paying accounts, and profitable usage.

What you will own

1. Go-to-market and customer acquisition

Identify our strongest initial customer segments, including AI startups, independent developers, agencies, and software teams.

Develop our positioning and explain why developers should choose Openbase.

Launch and improve acquisition across X, SEO, visibility in AI search engines, developer communities, partnerships, and targeted outbound.

Test paid campaigns with clear budgets, conversion tracking, and criteria for scaling or stopping.

Build a growth roadmap with weekly experiments and monthly acquisition targets.

2. Developer activation and retention

Own the journey from website visit to signup, first successful API request, first payment, and ongoing usage.

Work with engineering to remove onboarding friction and improve documentation, quickstarts, and integration examples.

Speak directly with developers to understand why they try Openbase, keep using it, or leave.

Establish onboarding communications, customer support processes, and reactivation campaigns.

Turn successful customer implementations into case studies and referrals.

3. Sales and partnerships

Personally source and close early customers.

Build a qualified pipeline of startups and businesses with recurring AI usage.

Develop distribution partnerships with developer tools, AI communities, accelerators, and complementary platforms.

Coordinate technical evaluations and customer requirements with engineering.

Build a repeatable sales process as demand grows.

4. Business execution and team management

Translate company goals into weekly priorities, accountable owners, and delivery dates.

Recruit and manage freelancers, agencies, and future hires across growth, content, developer relations, and customer success.

Own marketing budget allocation and evaluate spending against business results.

Coordinate customer needs with product and engineering priorities.

Implement practical workflows and automation that reduce manual work.

5. Metrics and commercial performance

Maintain a dashboard covering acquisition, activation, retention, paying customers, and API usage.

Track customer acquisition cost, conversion rates, and retention by channel.

Separate customer spending from provider costs and Openbase’s retained revenue and gross profit.

Monitor promotional credits and infrastructure costs so growth remains economically sound.

Give the founder a clear weekly view of results, blockers, and decisions needed.

What we are looking for

Experience leading growth and commercial execution at an early-stage SaaS, API, developer-tools, or AI infrastructure company.

Evidence of acquiring users from an early starting point, with specific numbers and your personal contribution.

Understanding of developer audiences and how technical products earn adoption.

Ability to understand an API integration, follow documentation, and discuss onboarding issues with engineers.

Hands-on ability to run experiments, analyze funnels, conduct customer calls, and manage delivery.

Experience managing budgets and external specialists.

Strong written English, sound judgment, and comfort working directly with a founder.

Experience with usage-based pricing, developer relations, technical SEO, and AI model platforms is particularly relevant.

Why join

Direct ownership of Openbase’s launch and growth.

Close collaboration with the founder and engineering team.

The opportunity to build the commercial function from its earliest stage.

Scope to take on broader company leadership as the business grows.

How to apply

Send your CV or LinkedIn profile, together with brief answers to:

Which product have you helped grow? Include starting users, ending users, timeframe, budget, and your exact role.

Which acquisition channels produced retained or paying customers?

How would you approach Openbase’s first 1,000 activated developers?

What would you personally execute, and where would you use specialists?

What are your location, availability, and compensation expectations?

Include an example of a growth experiment or operating system you built. Share only information you are authorized to disclose.

Headquarters: Victoria, British Columbia, Canada

The opportunity

I'm looking for an experienced operator to take ownership of a portfolio of three established Shopify apps with a combined ARR of approximately $1.87M.

The portfolio includes:

Geo:Pro: Geolocation-based storefront personalization

TrackiPal: PayPal tracking automation for Shopify merchants

Easy Lockdown: Content and storefront access control

Together, these are profitable, well-established products with engaged customer bases. They're not hypergrowth startups, but well-run businesses with clear opportunities to improve the product experience, strengthen operations and continue growing over time.

As the portfolio has grown, it's reached the point where I need an experienced operator to lead the day-to-day, keep the business running smoothly and turn strategy into execution.

The role is fully remote, async-friendly and suited to someone who enjoys ownership, autonomy and building well-run businesses.

What you'd own

Team coordination and delivery: Run the day-to-day by coordinating the developer and tester through the full delivery cycle - from spec → build → ship → measure - keeping everyone aligned across time zones and hiring additional contractors as needed.

Roadmap and prioritization: We'll set the roadmap together. I'll be closely involved at first, and over time this becomes increasingly your call. Turn Amplitude data, review themes and support signals into a prioritized backlog in Linear, and write clear tickets for the developer.

Metrics and experimentation: Own the analytics story. Understand what moved, what didn't and what to try next. Design experiments and report on impact.

Quality and documentation: Continually raise the bar on user experience through better documentation, smoother onboarding, fewer rough edges.

Platform stewardship: Stay ahead of Shopify API changes, manage App Store compliance reviews and lead our annual Built for Shopify review to retain BFS status.

Support oversight and escalations: Our support agency handles tier-1 tickets. You're the escalation point for product and engineering issues and own the agency relationship, ensuring response times, ticket quality and the merchant experience meet the bar.

Shopify App Store Paid Ads: Oversee existing paid advertising campaigns, working with our marketing contractor to ensure everything runs smoothly. We'll set the marketing budget together each quarter, and you'll manage it.

Shopify App Store rankings: Monitor Shopify App Store rankings across the portfolio, identify opportunities to improve rankings and respond quickly when rankings decline.

What you don't have to do

Write code (there's a developer for that)

Do QA (there's a tester for that)

Handle routine support tickets (an agency handles that)

Respond to reviews (a contractor handles that)

Fundraise, hire executives, sit in stakeholder meetings or manage political overhead - none of that exists here

Growth areas we've already identified

Easy Lockdown: Shift to usage-based pricing

Geo:Pro + Easy Lockdown: Onboarding and activation optimization

Geo:Pro + Easy Lockdown: Feature gaps that address missing customer use cases

All three apps: Lift review ratings to improve organic App Store rankings

You're not walking into a blank page - there's already a clear direction, but plenty of room to test your own ideas.

What you'll be walking into

Small, remote team: You'll be coordinating a small team of contractors working across different time zones, so communication and keeping work moving are a big part of the role.

Established products: The apps are profitable and well established, but some of the codebases are older and occasionally require pragmatic workarounds rather than perfect solutions.

Data-driven decisions: Our analytics stack is solid (Amplitude, BigQuery, Shopify Partners) - SQL fluency, or comfort writing it with AI help, is required.

How we'll work together

Founder involvement: I've run these apps alongside another business and know them inside out. I'll stay focused on product direction, strategy, quarterly planning and major decisions while you run the day-to-day.

Working rhythm: We'll meet weekly at first while we build context and alignment, then move to monthly strategy check-ins and quarterly planning sessions. Beyond that, you'll have the autonomy to run with it.

Who you are

Strong operator: You've successfully run product or delivery for a small SaaS team. Background isn't important - results are.

Technically fluent: You can write clear product specs, understand trade-offs and weigh development estimates without needing to review code.

Organized and proactive: You enjoy coordinating people, removing blockers and making sure nothing falls through the cracks.

Data-driven: You use Amplitude, SQL and customer feedback to inform decisions.

Self-directed: You're comfortable working asynchronously, managing your own priorities and taking ownership without constant direction.

Bonus: Experience in the Shopify ecosystem, App Store Optimization (ASO), paid acquisition or SaaS growth.

Where this could go

This isn't a role with a fixed ceiling. As you build context, take on more responsibility and the portfolio grows, there's scope for the role to grow too. Exactly what that looks like will depend on the business and the impact you have, but the door is genuinely open.

Role details

Time: Part-time, approximately 15-25 hours per week

Compensation: US$65-$85/hour, depending on experience

Employment: Contractor or employee - whichever works best for you

Location: Fully remote, async-friendly, any timezone

Start: As soon as you're available

How to apply

If this sounds like a role you'd enjoy, send me a 3-5 minute Loom walking me through how you'd approach your first 90 days. Assume you've had one week to get oriented - what would you focus on first, what would you want to understand, and how would you decide what to work on?

Email your Loom to: apply@geoproapp.com

I'll personally review every application. If your Loom is a strong fit, I'll invite you to a short introductory interview. If that goes well, we'll schedule a final, more in-depth interview before making an offer.

The Opportunity:

Our team develops the essential systems driving Grafana's business operations. What You’ll Be Doing:

The AppCore Stacks squad owns the systems that create, configure, reconcile, migrate, and operate Grafana Cloud stacks at scale. A stack is the customer-facing Grafana Cloud environment that connects an organization to Grafana and the backend services it uses, including Mimir, Loki, Tempo, plugins, dashboards, data sources, and stack-level configuration.

Our work sits at the intersection of product, platform, and operations.
